title: Identify Components and Resources for Security

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS provides different security services for different jobs, third-party products, security documentation, educational resources, and checks that identify security concerns.
sections.callout: Which AWS security service or security resource matches this need?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: LEARN → AWS security documentation and resources
sections.callout: FILTER → PROTECT → MANAGE → DETECT → ADVISE → LEARN

sections.title: AWS Security Capabilities
paragraphs: Security is a toolbox. A service that detects suspicious activity does not perform the same job as a web-request filter or centralized firewall-policy manager.
sections.callout: Recognize the job → choose the right tool.

entries.title: Security Groups
paragraphs: Stateful virtual firewalls associated with supported resources that control allowed inbound and outbound traffic.

entries.title: Network ACLs
paragraphs: Stateless traffic filters applied at the subnet boundary in an Amazon VPC.

entries.title: AWS WAF
paragraphs: A web application firewall that controls and filters HTTP or HTTPS web requests using rules.

entries.title: AWS Shield
paragraphs: Helps protect AWS workloads against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.

entries.title: AWS Firewall Manager
paragraphs: Centrally configures and manages firewall rules and security policies across multiple accounts and resources.

entries.title: Amazon GuardDuty
paragraphs: Continuously detects suspicious or potentially malicious activity using relevant AWS data sources.

sections.title: Third-Party Security Products — AWS Marketplace
paragraphs: AWS Marketplace provides software offerings from third-party vendors, including commercial security products that can be used with AWS environments.
sections.callout: Third-party cloud security software → AWS Marketplace

sections.title: AWS Security Documentation and Information
paragraphs: Sometimes the correct resource provides guidance rather than directly protecting a workload.

entries.title: AWS Knowledge Center
paragraphs: Answers and guidance for common AWS questions and technical issues.
entries.memoryHook: How do I understand or resolve this common issue?

entries.title: AWS Security Center
paragraphs: A destination for AWS security-related information and resources.

entries.title: AWS Security Blog
paragraphs: AWS-authored security articles, guidance, technical content, and updates.

sections.title: AWS Trusted Advisor
paragraphs: AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates AWS environments and provides best-practice recommendations across areas that include security. In this objective, recognize its role in identifying security issues and improvement opportunities.

table.caption: Give every security service or resource one clear job
rows: Filter traffic at a subnet boundary

entries.title: WAF vs. Shield
paragraphs: Filter web requests → WAF. DDoS protection → Shield.

entries.title: Security Group vs. Network ACL
paragraphs: Stateful control on supported resources → Security group. Stateless subnet-boundary filter → Network ACL.

entries.title: WAF vs. Firewall Manager
paragraphs: Apply web request rules → WAF. Centrally manage firewall and security policies → Firewall Manager.

entries.title: Shield vs. GuardDuty
paragraphs: DDoS protection → Shield. Threat detection → GuardDuty.

entries.title: GuardDuty vs. Inspector
paragraphs: Suspicious activity → GuardDuty. Software vulnerabilities and exposure → Inspector.

entries.title: GuardDuty vs. Trusted Advisor
paragraphs: Detect threats → GuardDuty. Recommend best-practice improvements → Trusted Advisor.

entries.title: Security Hub vs. Trusted Advisor
paragraphs: Centralize security findings → Security Hub. Best-practice recommendations → Trusted Advisor.

entries.title: AWS Service vs. Marketplace
paragraphs: AWS-provided capability → Specific AWS service. Third-party vendor security product → AWS Marketplace.
